newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi scraps China Beach permit after funding flap.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi scraps China Beach permit after funding flap.

text.p: Vietnam has withdrawn an American developer's licence to build a luxury holiday resort at the fabled China Beach after the company failed to make an initial deposit, the Ministry of Planning and Investment said on Friday.
Maryland-based BBI Investment Group was awarded a licence for the $243 million project, one of the biggest foreign-backed joint ventures in Vietnam, almost two years ago.

However, BBI and its local partner never got further than a groundbreaking ceremony at the central coast beach -- a former rest and recreation area for U.S. soldiers during the Vietnam War -- because of a tiff over funding.
BBI President Robert Bernstein told Reuters last month that he was unwilling to put more money into the project without certain assurance from Vietnamese officials.
"Until our concerns are addressed and met and resolved satisfactorily...we are not willing to invest any more money in this project," he said, without specifying the criteria for continued financing.
A ministry official said BBI had failed to meet contract requirements, notably by failing to lodge an initial deposit of $2 million and secure a loan for the whole project.
But Bernstein argued that BBI had spent more than $2 million directly on the project but had not channeled the money through the joint venture account because of bureaucratic difficulties.

Under the venture agreement signed in September 1994, BBI held a 67-percent interest in the venture. The rest was held by the Non Nuoc Tourist Co, set up by the People's Committee of Quang Nam-Danang province.

The ministry said the local partner was trying to estimate the losses, including opportunity costs, it had incurred as a result of the venture's failure. The Lao Dong newspaper put the figure at around $500,000.
The project was to have included the revamp of an existing beachfront hotel and the construction of a new hotel, golf course and related facilities on a 217-hectare (536-acre) area of land.
The daily Vietnam News recently quoted a senior official involved in the project as saying that at least three other foreign investors were willing to take BBI's place.
The ministry official confirmed that there had been interest from potential investors. "But this time we will be very careful about choosing a partner for that venture," he said.
